artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $I$ be an infinite set and let $D$ be a regular ultrafilter on $I$, i.e., an ultrafilter such that there exists a family $\{X_i : i \in I\} \subseteq D$ with the property that $\{i \in I : x \in X_i\}$ is finite for every $x$. For a monotonic function $f : [|I|]^{<\aleph_0} \to D$ (so $u \subseteq v$ implies $f(u) \supseteq f(v)$), a multiplicative refinement is a function $g : [|I|]^{<\aleph_0} \to D$ with $g(u) \subseteq f(u)$ and $g(u \cup v) = g(u) \cap g(v)$ for all finite $u, v$. The ultrafilter $D$ is called good if every monotonic $f : [|I|]^{<\aleph_0} \to D$ admits a multiplicative refinement.

For a regular cardinal $\kappa \le |I|$, say that $D$ has uniqueness for $\kappa$ if any two multiplicative refinements of any monotonic $f : [\kappa]^{<\aleph_0} \to D$ agree on a set in $D$ (i.e., the multiplicative refinement, when it exists, is essentially unique modulo $D$). Let $C(D)$ denote the set of monotonic functions $f : [|I|]^{<\aleph_0} \to D$ for which no multiplicative refinement exists; so $D$ is good if and only if $C(D) = \emptyset$.

Question: Does there exist a set $I$ and a regular ultrafilter $D$ on $I$ such that $D$ has uniqueness for every regular cardinal $\kappa \le |I|$, yet $C(D) \ne \emptyset$ (so $D$ is not good)?
artifact.status_search_result: No source was found indicating that the question of whether uniqueness (for all regular cardinals at most |I|) for a regular ultrafilter D on I is strictly weaker than goodness has been resolved. Related work by Malliaris and Shelah on ultrafilter constructions via independent families and on the canonical Boolean algebra is ongoing (including recent arXiv work in 2025), but does not appear to settle this specific problem. The status is best described as open.
